sentences.text: Court No. - 1 Case :- APPLICATION U/S 482 No. - 6242 of 2023 Applicant :- Vijay @ Vijay Singh Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 4 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Virendra Kumar Kori
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Pawan Kumar Patel Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State, counsel for the opposite party No. 2 and perused the record.

By means of this application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the applicant has challenged the entire criminal proceedings of Criminal Case No. 76 of 2021 (State vs. Vijay) arising out of Case Crime No.
139 of 2018, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, P.S. Bhutta, District- Bareilly, pending in the court of Addl.

sentences.text:
Brief facts giving rise to this application are that the first information report has been lodged by Mahendra Pal against the applicant on 29.5.2018 stating therein that on 19.5.2018 at about 12 a.m.
in the night, his daughter Km. Neeraj, who is a minor has illegally been enticed by the applicant- Vijay @ Vijay Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165752715/
1 Vijay @ Vijay Singh and when he woke up at about 12:30 a.m. in the night, his daughter was not in the house and when he had gone to enquire about his daughter then Charan Singh and Smt. Bebi wife of Nanhey threatened him not to lodge the report else would suffer huge losses to his family.

entities.text: Vijay @ Vijay Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the basis of said allegation, the first information report has been registered vide Case Crime No.
0139 of 2018, under Sections 363, 366 IPC.

After lodging of the FIR, the police thoroughly investigated the matter and after recording the statement of the witnesses and the relevant material regarding the age of the victim concluded the investigation and submitted the charge sheet against the applicant under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, vide charge sheet dated 9.12.2021.
On the basis of said charge sheet, the competent court has taken cognizance vide order dated 16.12.2021.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that during the pendency of the aforesaid proceedings before the court below, the parties have also entered into a compromise and, therefore,
in view of the compromise made between the parties, the entire proceedings be quashed.
Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the aforesaid prayer and has submitted that offence under Section 376 IPC and Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act are grave and non compoundable offences.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He has further drawn the attention of the Court to the recent decision of the Apex Court in the case of Daxaben vs. State of Gujarat, 2022 SCC online 936.

entities.text: Daxaben vs. State of Gujarat, 2022 SCC online 936
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further stated that heinous or serious crimes, which are not private in nature and have a serious impact upon society cannot be quashed on the basis of compromise between the offender and the complainant and/or the victim.
Crimes like murder, rape, burglary, dacoity are neither private nor civil in nature.
Such crimes are against the society.
In no circumstances can prosecution be quashed on compromise, when the offence is serious and grave and falls within the ambit of crime against society.

Orders quashing FIRs or complaints relating to grave and serious offences only on the basis of an agreement with the complainant would set a dangerous precedence, where complaints would be lodged for oblique reasons, with a view to extract money from the accused.

Furthermore, financially strong offenders would go scot free, even in cases of grave and serious offences such as murder, rape, bride burning etc. and would render otiose provisions such as sections 306, 304-B, 498A and 376 IPC and special offence under POCSO Act, which have been incorporated as a deterrent, with a specific social purpose.

In case of grave, serious non-compoundable offences, which impact society, the informant and/or complainant only has the right of hearing, to the extent of ensuring that justice is done by the conviction and punishment of the offender.
An informant has no right in law to withdraw the complaint of a non- compoundable offence of a grave, serious and/or heinous nature, which impacts society.

In respect of serious offences like murder, rape, dacoity etc., or other offences of mental depravity under IPC or serious offences under POCSO Act which are special statutes, the settlement between the offender and the victim can have no legal sanction at all.

sentences.text: In Narinder Singh & others vs. State of Punjab, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that in case of heinous and serious offences, which are generally treated to be crime against society, it is duty of the State to punish the offender.

entities.text: Narinder Singh & others vs. State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, even where there is a settlement the view of the offender and the victim will not prevail, since it is in the interest of the society that offender should be punished which would be deterrent for others, from committing similar crime.

Having considered the rival submission made by the parties and taking into account the settled principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in several of its decision particularly in the case of Narinder Singh & others vs. State of Punjab, 2014 (6) SCC 466 and Arun Singh and another vs. State of U.P. through its secretary reported in 2020 (3) SCC 736, I am of the view that in the instant case, proceeding cannot be quashed on the basis of compromise particularly under the POCSO Act, which is a special statute, the object of which is to Protect Children from Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment with due regard for safeguarding the interest and well being of children.

entities.text: Narinder Singh & others vs. State of Punjab, 2014 (6) SCC 466
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Arun Singh and another vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such offences need to be defined explicitly and countered through adequate penalties as an effective deterrence and in case such offences are quashed on the basis of compromise, the very object of passing the POCSO Act would become otiose and redundant.
In view of the foregoing discussion, I am of the view that in the instant case, the proceeding cannot be quashed on the basis of compromise.
The present application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is devoid of merit and is accordingly dismissed.
